references.title: Determining the rational points on a curve of genus 2 and Mordell-Weil rank 1
references.specific_section: Section 3, Algorithm 3.4 (local integral points, odd primes); Theorem 1.1 for scope
references.hypotheses: Local step: squarefree integral polynomial and odd prime. Full rational-point algorithm: known point generating a finite-index subgroup of a Jacobian of rank at most 1; general termination has stated conjectural hypotheses.
references.actual_use: Applied only the affine mod-5 obstruction step to the even sextic. Our curve has rational points at infinity, so projective local-solvability tests alone cannot exclude its integral locus. No full Chabauty/Mordell-Weil sieve was executed.

references.title: Linear quadratic Chabauty
references.specific_section: Appendix A, Theorem A.1 and Lemma A.2; main Theorem 1.1
references.hypotheses: Runge appendix: nonconstant squarefree even-degree integral polynomial with square leading coefficient. Main p-adic result: genus g, Jacobian rank g, prime of good reduction p>g.
references.actual_use: The v18 integer separation is an explicit instance of the appendix Runge mechanism. Used its proved a bound with exact local sieving and full reconstruction to exclude rho<=10. The p-adic-height algorithm is not executed, and ranks are not known uniformly.

references.title: Affine Chabauty II
references.specific_section: Introduction inequality(1.1), Section1.2 algorithm, Section5.1 even hyperelliptic curves
references.hypotheses: For K=Q, genus2, two rational boundary points and S empty, the numerical rank condition is rank(J)<3. Also assumes an affine rational base point, a regular model, bad-fiber intersection data, full-rank Mordell-Weil subgroup and Coleman log integrals. The chosen regular integral model must cover the original integer solutions.
references.actual_use: Assessed applicability to our genus2 fibers. The necessary numerical rank condition and required geometric/arithmetic inputs are not supplied uniformly. The rational infinity points do not provide an affine base point. No run of the authors’ Sage implementation is claimed.

references.title: Modular Chabauty: Effective S-Integral Point Computation On Curves with Elliptic Fibrations
references.specific_section: Definition1.3 and Algorithm2.1; fixed-S effective Shafarevich step
references.hypotheses: A geometrically connected curve over Z[1/S] with a non-isotrivial elliptic scheme, for a specified finite S.
references.actual_use: Computed actual discriminant and c4. Every fixed-(a,b) fiber with a>b, gcd(a,b)=1,b|486 has a multiplicative bad prime >=5. The possible supports are not bounded by b|486, so S={2,3} is not justified. No implementation run.

references.title: Number of integral points on quadratic twists of elliptic curves
references.hypotheses: A fixed rational elliptic curve, its quadratic twists by sufficiently large positive squarefree D; conclusion bounds the number of integral points in terms of rank.
references.actual_use: Not directly applicable to the whole residual family: its j-invariant varies. A count bound would not itself determine every point.

references.title: Catalogue of GP/PARI Functions: Elliptic curves
references.hypotheses: ellrank/elltors for a rational elliptic curve; ellrank reports algebraic rank bounds.
references.actual_use: Separate real GP experiment on 45 fixed-(b,rho) curves. Rank-zero upper bounds and torsion order3 imply no admissible solution by Theorem2. Not an input to the independent standard-Python certificate. No ellanalyticrank/BSD or ellratpoints height search.

references.title: 18.782 Introduction to Arithmetic Geometry, Lecture24
references.hypotheses: Nonsingular short Weierstrass equation over Q with integer coefficients; rational affine torsion point.
references.actual_use: Primary university lecture notes checked while independently reviewing the root reviewer’s separate uniform non-torsion theorem. That theorem is not reproduced or assumed in this finite certificate.
